catalyst_text: Received FDA IND clearance to begin Phase 1
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA cleared the IND application to initiate a Phase 1 trial of DYNE-302 in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy. This regulatory acceptance enables first-in-human testing and advances the program into clinical development.
catalyst_text_evidence: Dyne Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:DYN) ... today announced that it has received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its IND application to initiate a Phase 1 clinical trial for DYNE-302 in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD).

drug_indication: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy amenable to exon 51 skipping
catalyst_text: BLA accepted Priority Review granted PDUFA January 2027
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted the BLA for treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy amenable to exon 51 skipping and granted Priority Review. A PDUFA target action date of 2027-01-21 was assigned. This acceptance under Priority Review expedites evaluation and marks a key regulatory milestone toward potential accelerated approval.
catalyst_text_evidence: Dyne Therapeutics, Inc. ... announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted for review the Biologics License Application (BLA) for zeleciment rostudirsen (z-rostudirsen, also known as DYNE-251) for the treatment of individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 51 skipping. The FDA has granted the BLA Priority Review and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of January 21, 2027. Submission for Accelerated Approval based on dystrophin as a surrogate endpoint.

catalyst_text: Completed enrollment of registrational expansion cohort in DM1
detailed_catalyst_text: Announced completion of enrollment in the registrational expansion cohort of the Phase 1/2 ACHIEVE trial in myotonic dystrophy type 1, totaling 71 participants. This fully enrolled cohort is intended to support potential regulatory submissions, including U.S. Accelerated Approval.
catalyst_text_evidence: Dyne Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:DYN), a clinical-stage company focused on delivering functional improvement for people living with genetically driven neuromuscular diseases, today announced the completion of enrollment in the registrational expansion cohort (REC) of the Phase 1/2 ACHIEVE trial of zeleciment basivarsen (z-basivarsen, also known as DYNE-101) in individuals with DM1. A registrational expansion cohort to support potential regulatory submissions, including Accelerated Approval in the U.S., is fully enrolled. Registrational expansion cohort enrolled 71 participants; topline data planned for Q1 2027.

catalyst_text: Submitted BLA supported by robust positive clinical results
detailed_catalyst_text: A Biologics License Application was submitted to the FDA for exon 51–amenable Duchenne muscular dystrophy with a 20 mg/kg Q4W regimen. The application seeks Accelerated Approval and is supported by DELIVER registrational expansion cohort data showing robust, statistically significant dystrophin increases with functional improvement and a favorable safety profile. A Priority Review request accompanied the filing.
catalyst_text_evidence: Dyne Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:DYN)... today announced the submission of a Biologics License Application (BLA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for zeleciment rostudirsen (z-rostudirsen, also known as DYNE-251) 20 mg/kg Q4W for the treatment of individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 51 skipping. In the registrational expansion cohort of the DELIVER trial, treatment with z-rostudirsen resulted in a robust and statistically significant increase in dystrophin production with functional improvement observed across multiple clinical endpoints and a favorable safety profile1. Data from the DELIVER trial served as the basis for a Biologics License Application (BLA) for potential U.S. Accelerated Approval. Dyne has requested Priority Review for the BLA, which, if granted, would shorten the review process from 10 months to 6 months following the FDA's 60-day filing review period.

catalyst_text: Initiated global randomized confirmatory Phase 3 trial enrollment
detailed_catalyst_text: A Phase 3 trial in myotonic dystrophy type 1 was initiated, with first sites activated and open for enrollment. The randomized, placebo-controlled study is aligned with FDA on design and protocol and is positioned as a confirmatory trial.
catalyst_text_evidence: Dyne Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:DYN), a clinical-stage company focused on delivering functional improvement for people living with genetically driven neuromuscular diseases, today announced the initiation of the Phase 3 HARMONIA trial of zeleciment basivarsen (z-basivarsen, also known as DYNE-101), in individuals with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1). The first trial sites are activated and open to enrollment. Dyne has aligned with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on the HARMONIA Phase 3 trial design and protocol.

catalyst_text: Presented positive 24 month cardiopulmonary data at conference
detailed_catalyst_text: Additional analyses from the ongoing Phase 1/2 DELIVER trial in Duchenne muscular dystrophy amenable to exon 51 skipping showed improvements in pulmonary and cardiac function through 24 months versus expected natural history declines. The findings were presented in a late-breaking poster at the Muscular Dystrophy Association 2026 meeting and expand on prior reports of sustained functional benefit. These results highlight potential for broad muscle, including cardiopulmonary, improvement.
catalyst_text_evidence: Dyne Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:DYN) ... today announced additional positive data from the ongoing Phase 1/2 DELIVER clinical trial of zeleciment rostudirsen (z-rostudirsen, also known as DYNE-251), in individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 51 skipping. These data are being presented in a late-breaking poster presentation at the 2026 Muscular Dystrophy Association (MDA) Clinical & Scientific Conference being held March 8-11, 2026, in Orlando, FL, which is available in the Scientific Publications & Presentations section of Dyne's website along with all of Dyne's other posters being presented at the conference. Improvement from baseline in lung function, as measured by Forced Vital Capacity Percent Predicted (FVC%p), was observed through 24 months, as compared to the expected decline estimated in published natural history data2-4. Improvement from baseline was observed through 24 months in circumferential strain, an early signal of cardiac performance, as compared to the expected worsening estimated in published natural history data5,6. Improvement from baseline in left ventricular ejection fraction, a measure of how well the heart is pumping, was observed at 24 months, in contrast with the expected decline estimated in published natural history data5,6.

catalyst_text: Received orphan drug designation in Japan for DM1
detailed_catalyst_text: Japan’s MHLW granted Orphan Drug designation to z-basivarsen for myotonic dystrophy type 1. The program is being studied in the global Phase 1/2 ACHIEVE trial. This designation provides development incentives and potential market exclusivity in Japan if approved, supporting the regulatory path.
catalyst_text_evidence: Dyne Therapeutics, Inc. ... today announced that the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) in Japan has granted Orphan Drug designation for zeleciment basivarsen (z-basivarsen), for the treatment of myotonic muscular dystrophy type 1 (DM1). Z-basivarsen is currently being evaluated in the Phase 1/2 ACHIEVE clinical trial in individuals with DM1. ... Benefits include subsidies for development costs and potential market exclusivity for up to 10 years if approved.

catalyst_text: Trial met primary endpoint with significant dystrophin increase
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline results from the Phase 1/2 DELIVER Registrational Expansion Cohort showed the primary endpoint was met in individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy amenable to exon 51 skipping. Muscle content–adjusted dystrophin increased to 5.46% at six months with favorable safety, functional improvements across multiple endpoints, and preserved lung function versus placebo. New long-term OLE/LTE data demonstrated sustained functional improvement across assessed endpoints out to 24 months, strengthening the efficacy and durability profile.
catalyst_text_evidence: WALTHAM, Mass., 2025-12-08 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dyne Therapeutics, Inc. ... today announced positive topline results from the Registrational Expansion Cohort (REC) of its Phase 1/2 DELIVER trial evaluating zeleciment rostudirsen (z-rostudirsen, also known as DYNE-251) in individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 51 skipping. The REC met its primary endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant increase in muscle content-adjusted dystrophin expression to 5.46% of normal relative to baseline at six months (p<0.0001). In addition, improvement relative to placebo was observed across all six prespecified functional endpoints from the topline readout of the REC. Importantly, lung function, the loss of which is a leading cause of mortality in DMD, as measured by Forced Vital Capacity Percent Predicted (FVC%p), was preserved at 6 months compared to a decline in placebo. Additionally, Dyne announced new positive long-term clinical data from the ongoing open-label extension (OLE) and long-term extension (LTE) portions of DELIVER. Sustained functional improvement in TTR Velocity, 10MWR Velocity, NSAA, SV95C, PUL2.0, and FVC%p from baseline were observed ... out to 24 months.
